Bug Report

Item Detail
Confirmed bug Min/max dimension validation rejects correctly, but response messages do not match the issue acceptance contract.
Expected min-size message Image resolution is too low. Minimum required size is 400x400 pixels.
Expected max-size message Image resolution is too high. Maximum allowed size is 2048x2048 pixels.

Validation logic is working: the API correctly rejects images below 400x400 and above 2048x2048. The bug is only in the returned error text. issues.display_title: Issue #1606: Fix Bug "Failed to upload avatar" Error on Photographer Profile for New Accounts
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Users with newly created accounts are unable to upload a logo/avatar on their Photographer Profile page. When attempting to drag and drop or click to upload an image into the designated area, the upload fails and triggers a red toast notification stating: "Failed to upload avatar".

User Notes & Workaround Attempt

The user suspected the account might need an initial activity trigger to initialize storage space, so they tried creating a virtual tour and successfully uploaded a 360 image to that tour. However, returning to the profile page and attempting the avatar upload still resulted in the exact same failure.

Test File Used

A standard 360 view logo (PNG/JPG) was used for the upload attempt, ruling out an obscure file type issue.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. New accounts can successfully upload an avatar/logo to their profile immediately after registration.
  2. The avatar upload process functions independently and does not require the user to create a tour or perform other actions to "unlock" or initialize their storage.
  3. If an upload fails due to validation (size/format), the UI displays a clear and accurate reason to the user.

Test Scenario (for Tester / QA)

Preconditions

  • Have (or create) a brand-new account that has performed no other activity (no tours, no uploads).
  • Open browser DevTools -> Network/Console to capture the failing avatar upload request/response.
  • Have a valid avatar image ready (standard PNG/JPG within allowed size).

Scenario 1 - Fresh account avatar upload (the bug)

  1. Register a new account and go directly to Photographer Profile.
  2. Upload an avatar/logo via drag-and-drop and again via click-to-upload.
  3. Expected: The avatar uploads successfully and displays on the profile - no "Failed to upload avatar" toast.
  4. Bug (before fix): Red toast "Failed to upload avatar" appears; avatar is not saved.

Scenario 2 - No tour-creation dependency

  1. On a fresh account that has never created a tour, upload the avatar first (before any other action).
  2. Expected: Upload works without needing to create a tour or upload a 360 image first (the storage-init workaround must not be required).

Scenario 3 - Persistence after reload

  1. After a successful avatar upload, reload the profile page (and re-login).
  2. Expected: The avatar persists and is shown consistently.

Scenario 4 - Validation error messaging

  1. Attempt to upload an oversized file and an unsupported format (e.g. .bmp/.svg/.txt).
  2. Expected: Upload is rejected with a clear, accurate reason (e.g. "File too large (max X MB)" / "Unsupported format - use PNG or JPG") - not a generic "Failed to upload avatar".

Scenario 5 - Update existing avatar

  1. Upload a new avatar to replace an existing one.
  2. Expected: The new image replaces the old one successfully.

Scenario 6 - Regression on established accounts

  1. Repeat the avatar upload on an older/established account.
  2. Expected: Still works - the fix doesn't regress accounts that already worked.

Pass criteria: A brand-new account can upload an avatar immediately with no workaround; failures only occur for genuine validation issues and show a clear, specific message.

issues.display_title: Issue #2069: feat(auth): magic link (passwordless email) sign-in API
issues.main_description_html:
Background

When Single Sign-On (Keycloak) is down, the dashboard shows a fallback login
(GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4392). One of its options is a sign-in link sent
to the user's email. The dashboard side is built, but it runs on a mock because
there is no API yet.

Goal

Users with a GoThru account can sign in with a link sent to their email,
without a password.

Scope

  • POST /v1/auth/magic-link: sends a sign-in link to the email.
    • An unregistered email gets 404 "User not found"; a blocked account is
      rejected.
    • The link is valid for 15 minutes and can only be used once. Requesting a
      new link cancels the previous one.
    • The link only points to approved dashboard addresses (allowlist).
    • Limits: one request per email per 60 seconds, and at most 5 requests per
      email per hour.
  • POST /v1/auth/magic-link/verify: checks the link and logs the user in.
    • Returns the same response as the other logins (token + session cookie).
    • An unverified account is activated, since clicking the link proves the
      user owns the email.
    • A blocked account is rejected.
  • The email is sent with a Plunk template, with these variables:
    magic_link_url, expires_in_minutes, email, year.

Out of Scope

  • Designing the email template and its wording (separate task).
  • Registering new accounts by magic link.
  • Per-IP limits (the API doesn't read the real client IP behind the proxy yet).
  • Dashboard changes beyond switching off the mock.

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: A registered email gets an email with a sign-in link; the
    response is 200.
  • AC-002: An unregistered email gets 404 "User not found", and no email
    is sent. A blocked account gets 422. If the email can't be sent, the
    response is 503 and the user can try again straight away.
  • AC-003: A redirect_url that isn't on the allowlist is rejected (422).
  • AC-004: A second request within 60 seconds, or a 6th within an hour, is
    rejected (429).
  • AC-005: A valid link logs the user in and returns the token + session
    cookie.
  • AC-006: A link that is wrong, expired (over 15 minutes), already used,
    or replaced by a newer link is rejected (401).
  • AC-007: An unverified account is activated when the link is opened; a
    blocked account is rejected (422).
  • AC-008: Unit tests cover AC-001 – AC-007.

Dependencies

  • Email template task (#2070): the template ID goes into
    EmailTemplateUID::MAGIC_LINK. Until then sending fails, so a registered
    email gets 503.

Related

  • GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4392: fallback login (frontend)
  • GoThruMedia/gothru-dashboard#4393: fallback login PR

Result

Shipped in #2071 (merged 2026-10-20, d78f251). All acceptance criteria AC-001 – AC-008 passed.

  • POST /v1/auth/magic-link: emails a one-time sign-in link (15 min TTL, single use, a new request revokes the previous link). Only the sha256 of the token is stored in Redis.
  • POST /v1/auth/magic-link/verify: exchanges the token for a GT token + session cookie, the same response shape as /auth/login.
  • Link URL uses only the origin of redirect_url, and only if it's in MAGIC_LINK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS; the path is always /auth/magic-link.
  • Per-email limits: 60s cooldown, max 5 requests per hour.
  • Error responses: 404 unregistered email, 422 blocked account / origin not on the allowlist, 429 over the limit, 401 invalid / expired / used / replaced link, 503 email send failure (token dropped and cooldown released so the user can retry right away).
  • Email template (#2070): EmailTemplateUID::MAGIC_LINK is filled in the same PR, so the Dependencies item is resolved. The template uses magic_link_url, expires_in_minutes and email; year isn't used.
  • Unit tests: MagicLinkRequestActionTest, MagicLinkVerifyActionTest, MagicLinkUrlHelperTest, MagicLinkTokenRepositoryTest.
  • Docs: docs/v2/auth/magic-link-request.md, docs/v2/auth/magic-link-verify.md, docs/REGISTERED_APIS.md, plus API collection entries (api-collection/GoThru API NEW/Auth/).

Deploy note: requires the env MAGIC_LINK_ALLOWED_ORIGINS (comma-separated dashboard origins); if it's empty, every request fails with 422.

Background

The magic link sign-in API (#2069) sends users an email containing a one-time sign-in link. The email needs a template in Plunk.

Goal

Users receive a clear, trustworthy email that lets them sign in with one click, and that tells them what to do if they didn't request it.

Scope

  • Template in Plunk (type Transactional, so the email reaches unsubscribed contacts and has no unsubscribe footer), in the same style as the existing GoThru emails (e.g. the archive tour failed email).
  • Plunk template ID: dddc81cd-cb93-449f-bd1f-6c873597624a
  • Variables used by the template:
    • magic_link_url: the sign-in link (button + plain-text fallback link)
    • expires_in_minutes: how long the link is valid (currently 15)
    • email: the recipient's email
  • The API also sends year, but the template doesn't use it. The year footer was replaced by the standard GoThru signature and contact block.
  • Put the template ID into EmailTemplateUID::MAGIC_LINK in the API (on the #2069 branch, PR #2071).

Wording

Subject: Your GoThru sign-in link

Hi,

Click the button below to sign in to GoThru as {{email}}.

[ Sign in to GoThru ] ({{magic_link_url}})

If the button doesn't work, copy and paste this link into your browser: {{magic_link_url}}

This link expires in {{expires_in_minutes}} minutes and can only be used once. If it has expired, you can request a new one from the sign-in page.

If you didn't try to sign in, you can ignore this email. Your account is safe and nobody can sign in without this link.

Regards,
GoThru Media Team

Phone: (800) 461-2405
YouTube: https://goo.gl/v2tUkl

issues.display_title: Issue #2076: fix(payment): Photo Studio subscribe returns subscription_plan_not_found (User 31611)
issues.main_description_html:
Problem Description

QA reported that subscribing to the Photo Studio plan as User 31611 fails, and the API returns messages.tours.subscription_plan_not_found (HTTP 409).

User

  • User ID: 31611
  • The user is in the Stripe test user list (HelperClass::getStripeTestUserIds()), so the subscribe flow runs in Stripe test mode and reads the *_test plan IDs.

Possible Sources

The error is thrown in several places. Need to confirm which one this request hits:

  • SubscriptionClass::addSubscription(): plan key not found in the Redis Stripe plans (test mode).
  • PaymentHelpers::getPlanDetails(): Photo Studio product not found or amount <= 0 (e.g. one_time_payment = 1, because photo_studio / photo_studio_year only map to a product for recurring).
  • PaymentHelpers::getPlanDetails(): product row has no plan_stripe_test / plan_paypal_test plan ID.
  • PayPal CreateSubscription paths, if the subscribe went through PayPal.

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: Find which endpoint, payload (plan, one_time_payment, processor) and throw site produce the error for User 31611.
  • AC-002: Root cause identified with evidence (code path + product / plan data).
  • AC-003: Fix applied (code or data). If it's data only (e.g. a missing test plan ID), document the exact change needed.
  • AC-004: Check whether non-test users and both Photo Studio Monthly / Yearly are affected too.
  • AC-005: User 31611 can subscribe to Photo Studio successfully.

Result

Root cause (AC-001, AC-002)

  • Endpoint: POST /v2/payment/subscription/subs (Stripe). User 31611 has user_extra_data.one_time_payment = 1.
  • PaymentHelpers::getPlanDetails() calls HelperClass::getProductIdByName('photo_studio', 1). photo_studio / photo_studio_year only mapped for recurring (subscriptionType = 0), so it returned 0 → subscription_plan_not_found (409).
  • Affects every user with one_time_payment = 1, for both Monthly and Yearly (AC-004). Recurring users were not affected.

Fix (AC-003)

  • Data: one-time products 46 / 47 added to ccdb.product (#2085), and ccdb.cc_purchase.product_id enum extended to '47' (#2086). Both done on production; staging uses the same ccdb.
  • Code: Gitea PR #2093 → staging (commits 1ff9ab1a7, 880834117)
    • ProductID::PHOTO_STUDIO_ONE_TIME = 46, PHOTO_STUDIO_YEAR_ONE_TIME = 47; getProductIdByName maps them for subscriptionType = 1.
    • Cron process-unsubscribes-photo-studio-table Flow 2 moved to PhotoStudioUnsubscribesSweeper and only processes rows with next_payment_date < today. Before, a one-time buyer lost access on the next cron run.
    • ClaimTrial purchase history and the Photo Studio hard reset include 46 / 47.
  • Behavior change: recurring Photo Studio unsubscribe / downgrade rows are now processed after the end of the period, not on the next cron run.

issues.display_title: Issue #2078: feat(auth): email OTP (6-digit code) sign-in API
issues.main_description_html:
Background

Users can already sign in without a password through a magic link sent to their email (#2069), but that flow is for the website: the link opens a dashboard page in the browser. The desktop and mobile apps can't take over from a link opened in the browser, so they need a code the user types into the app instead.

Goal

Users with a GoThru account can sign in to the desktop and mobile apps with a 6-digit code sent to their email, without a password. The magic link stays the passwordless option for the website.

Scope

  • POST /v1/auth/otp: sends a 6-digit sign-in code to the email.
    • An unregistered email gets 404; a blocked account is rejected.
    • The code is valid for 15 minutes and can only be used once. Requesting a new code cancels the previous one.
    • Limits: one request per email per 60 seconds, and at most 5 requests per email per hour (separate from the magic link limits).
    • The response returns expires_in and resend_in so the app can show a countdown.
  • POST /v1/auth/otp/verify: checks email + code and logs the user in.
    • Returns the same response as the other logins (token + session cookie).
    • After 5 wrong codes the code is cancelled and the user must request a new one.
    • An unverified account is activated, since knowing the code proves the user owns the email.
    • A blocked account is rejected.
  • Only a hash of the code is stored; the code is never logged.
  • The email is sent with a Plunk template, with these variables: otp_code, expires_in_minutes.

Out of Scope

  • Designing the email template and its wording (#2079).
  • Desktop and mobile app screens for entering the code (separate tasks per app).
  • Using the code on the website (the website keeps the magic link).
  • Registering new accounts by code.
  • Per-IP limits (the API doesn't read the real client IP behind the proxy yet).

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: A registered email gets an email with a 6-digit code; the response is 200 with expires_in and resend_in.
  • AC-002: An unregistered email gets 404 and no email is sent. A blocked account gets 422. If the email can't be sent, the response is 503 and the user can try again straight away.
  • AC-003: A second request within 60 seconds, or a 6th within an hour, is rejected (429).
  • AC-004: A correct code logs the user in and returns the token + session cookie.
  • AC-005: A code that is wrong, expired (over 15 minutes), already used, or replaced by a newer code is rejected (401).
  • AC-006: After 5 wrong codes the next attempt is rejected (429), and even the correct code no longer works until a new one is requested.
  • AC-007: An unverified account is activated when the code is verified; a blocked account is rejected (422).
  • AC-008: Unit tests cover AC-001 – AC-007.

Dependencies

  • Email template (#2079): its UID 6c471406-68a1-4ba8-9878-ce346c9d298a is set in EmailTemplateUID::LOGIN_OTP (commit 5aaf43872, PR #2077).

Related

  • #2069: magic link sign-in API
  • #2077: this feature's PR

Result

Implementation

  • PR: #2077 (merged into main 2026-10-22, bee7c7cb1). It's shared with #2079, the email template.
  • Commits:
    • c9859e2a0 feat(auth): add 6-digit email OTP login (POST /v1/auth/otp, /otp/verify)
    • 5aaf43872 feat(email): set Plunk template ID for login OTP email (#2079)
    • 0dea174a2 feat(auth): extend login OTP expiry to 15 minutes (#2078)
  • POST /v1/auth/otp: emails a 6-digit code (15 min TTL, single use; a new request cancels the previous code). Returns { expires_in: 900, resend_in: 60 }. Only sha256(email|code) is stored in Redis (login_otp:* keys); the code is never logged.
  • POST /v1/auth/otp/verify: exchanges email + code for a GT token + session cookie, the same response shape as /auth/login. After 5 wrong codes the code is cancelled.
  • Per-email limits: 60s cooldown, max 5 requests per hour (separate from the magic link limits).
  • Error responses: 404 unregistered email, 422 blocked account, 429 over the limit / too many wrong codes, 401 invalid / expired / used / replaced code, 503 email send failure (code dropped and cooldown released so the user can retry right away).
  • Email template (#2079): EmailTemplateUID::LOGIN_OTP = 6c471406-68a1-4ba8-9878-ce346c9d298a. The API sends only otp_code and expires_in_minutes.
  • Unit tests: OtpRequestActionTest, OtpVerifyActionTest, OtpCodeRepositoryTest, EmailTemplateUIDTest.
  • API collection: Auth/OTP Request and Auth/OTP Verify (api-collection/GoThru API NEW/Auth/).

Testing

  • E2E test by the developer: passed. All acceptance criteria AC-001 – AC-008 passed.

Follow-ups (not blocking)

  • No daily cap on wrong codes per email: with 5 tries per code and 5 codes per hour, about 600 guesses per day are possible. A daily lockout would close this.
  • All limits are keyed by email only, so someone who knows a user's email can use up that user's attempts and requests.

issues.display_title: Issue #2084: fix(centering-tool): "Failed to get image dimensions" for panorama 47842960
issues.main_description_html:
Problem Description

Users report an error when centering/rotating a panorama in the moderator (centering tool API, CenteringTool::execute):

Failed to get image dimensions for panorama ID: 47842960 (file may be corrupted or invalid image format)

The error is thrown in RollImageClass::rollPanoImage(). The full image path is not empty, the file exists and is readable, but HelperClass::getImageDimensions() returns false.

Panorama

  • Pano ID: 47842960
  • Moderation / user: TBD (from the server log line RollImageClass::rollPanoImage - FAILED to get image dimensions. PanoId: 47842960 ...)

Notes

  • getImageDimensions() runs /usr/bin/identify -format "%w %h" <file> 2>&1 and discards ImageMagick's output on failure, so the real reason is not logged.
  • This failed before with getimagesize() too. Retries were added (36d7a29b8), then it was switched to identify (f835f675c). Neither fixed it.
  • Possible causes:
    • the file is corrupted, truncated, or not a JPEG
    • the pano_rotate worker is still rewriting the same file from a previous rotation
    • ImageMagick policy.xml width/area limits block large panoramas
  • Side effect: with rotate_all, fixAnglesForOnePano() runs before rollPanoImage(). A pano that fails here still gets its new fov saved to the DB, even though its image was never rotated.

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: Root cause for pano 47842960 identified with evidence (file info, identify output, server log).
  • AC-002: getImageDimensions() logs the real ImageMagick error when it fails.
  • AC-003: Fix applied (code or data). If it's data only (e.g. a broken file), document what's needed to recover it.

Result

Root cause (confirmed by a production test on 2026-10-23)

  • HelperClass::getImageDimensions() ran identify without -ping, so ImageMagick decoded the whole panorama just to read its width. On production that decode fails for panoramas of roughly 50 MP and up (the limit is between 32 MP and 50 MP). The function then returned false, and RollImageClass::rollPanoImage() threw "Failed to get image dimensions". Panorama 47842960 is 11904 × 5952 (70.9 MP).
  • The file is a valid JPEG. Metadata, JPEG type, the user and the tour play no role. It looked user-specific because only users with high-resolution panoramas are affected.
  • The old code also dropped ImageMagick's error message, so the cause never showed up in the logs.

Production test (regular account, new tour, current production code, synthetic panoramas with the same JPEG spec: baseline, q95, 4:2:0, XMP GPano)

Panorama Pixels Result
5760 × 2880 16.6 MP ✅
8000 × 4000 32.0 MP ✅
10000 × 5000 50.0 MP ❌ same error
11904 × 5952 (same spec, progressive, low detail, no metadata) 70.9 MP ❌ same error, all four
13600 × 6800 92.5 MP ❌ same error
16384 × 8192 134.2 MP ❌ same error

Implementation

  • Branch: fix/centering-image-dimensions-2084 (pushed, no PR yet).
  • Commits:
    • b509bd88a fix(helper): read image dimensions from header and log identify errors (#2084)
    • 2e1297d53 docs(investigations): centering tool image dimensions root cause and mitigation (#2084)
  • getImageDimensions():
    • identify -ping: reads the header only, so there is no decode and no size limit (on the devbox, a 70.9 MP panorama drops from ~558 MB / ~650 ms to ~11 MB / ~10 ms).
    • stdout and stderr are read separately, so ImageMagick warnings can't be parsed as the result.
    • A result is accepted only when the exit code is 0 and width and height are > 0.
    • Failures are logged with Log::warning('[HelperClass::getImageDimensions] identify failed', [...]), including path, file_size, exit_code, output and ImageMagick's error.
  • Unit tests: tests/Class/HelperClassGetImageDimensionsTest.php, not run yet.
  • Investigation doc: docs/investigations/2026-10-23-centering-tool-image-dimensions.md

Acceptance criteria status

  • AC-001: done (root cause with production evidence, see above).
  • AC-002: implemented in b509bd88a, not deployed.
  • AC-003: fix committed, not merged or deployed.

Follow-ups

  • After deploy, re-test the 50 MP+ panoramas and check that the image is actually rotated (thumbnail and version change). The pano_rotate worker also decodes the full image, so if it has a similar limit, the API would accept the request but the rotation would not happen.
  • DevOps: run identify -list resource, free -m and df -h /tmp on the API and worker servers to get the exact limit.
  • Dashboard Centering.jsx: the modal stays stuck in loading when version polling times out after 5 s.
  • rotate_all: call rollPanoImage() before fixAnglesForOnePano().

Deploy status: not merged, not on production.

issues.display_title: Issue #2087: fix(payment): subscription status ignores past_due for users with a cus_ recurring_profile
issues.main_description_html:
Problem Description

GET /v2/payment/subscription/status (app/Http/Controllers/Payment/Actions/GetSubStatus.php) only retrieves the Stripe subscription when user_extra_data.recurring_profile starts with sub (L99). Users whose recurring_profile holds a Stripe customer ID (cus_…) are skipped, so the endpoint always returns the defaults: is_past_due = false, subscription = false, nextPayment = null, status = active, collection_method = charge_automatically.

Because of this, the dashboard dunning gate (useDunningGate) never blocks paid features or shows the dunning modal for these users, even when their Stripe subscription is past_due.

Example

  • User 1001: recurring_profile = cus_LMvBClkhuDwJxr, subscription sub_1KgBMA4UXotNjjkIVXiQiGEy (send_invoice, Pro $34/month).

Expected

When recurring_profile is a cus_… ID, look up the customer's subscription on Stripe and use it to build the status response. recurring_profile stays as it is.

Notes

  • The recurring cron already resolves cus_ profiles to subscriptions (StripeFailedPaymentDetector, RecordStripeRecurringTransactionsHelper).

Acceptance Criteria

  • AC-001: For a cus_… profile, the endpoint finds the customer's subscription and returns the same fields as for a sub_… profile (subscription, nextPayment, status, is_past_due, collection_method, amount_due, currency).
  • AC-002: If the customer has more than one subscription, the endpoint uses the live one (active / past_due / unpaid / trialing), not just the newest.
  • AC-003: If the customer has no live subscription, the response stays the same as today (defaults) and no error is returned.
  • AC-004: user_extra_data.recurring_profile is not modified.
  • AC-005: Unit tests cover a cus_… profile with a past_due subscription, with multiple subscriptions, and with no subscription.

Result

Shipped in PR #2100 (Gitea) (merged into staging 2026-10-29, 3b712777b). All acceptance criteria AC-001 – AC-005 passed.

  • recurring_profile is only read, never updated.
  • Data check (2026-10-29, live Stripe): 33 users have a cus_ profile. Each customer has exactly one subscription (all statuses counted), all active, so none of them is currently past due.
  • Unit tests (tests/Actions/Payment/GetSubStatusTest.php): cus_ with a past_due subscription, with multiple subscriptions (newest not live), with no subscription, and with a customer missing on Stripe, plus the 2 existing sub_ tests. All 6 pass.

issues.display_title: Issue #2088: feat(payment): flag send_invoice subscriptions as past due while the latest invoice is open

Problem Description

For subscriptions with collection_method = send_invoice, Stripe only moves the subscription to past_due after the invoice due date (period start + days_until_due, 30 days on this account).
